questions.q: Why doesn't spark.read.parquet() need a header or inferSchema flag?
options: Because Spark ignores schemas entirely for Parquet files
Because Parquet already stores its own schema inside the file itself, at write time
Because Parquet files never have column names
Because Parquet always uses generic column names like _c0, _c1
questions.explain: This is called schema-on-write — the schema is already known, not guessed on every read.

questions.q: How is data physically stored in a Parquet file, compared to CSV?
options: As a single unstructured blob with no internal layout
Identically to CSV, just with a different file extension
Column by column, rather than row by row like CSV
Row by row, exactly like CSV
questions.explain: CSV stores every field of a row together; Parquet stores every value of a column together.

questions.q: Why can selecting just 2 columns out of 50 be much faster from Parquet than from CSV?
options: Parquet's columnar layout lets Spark read only the bytes for those 2 columns off disk, while CSV must read every field of every row regardless
CSV files cannot be filtered by column at all
Parquet files are always stored in memory already
There's no actual difference in read speed between the two formats
questions.explain: This is the core practical benefit of columnar storage for analytics workloads that only touch a subset of columns.

questions.q: Why did the NYC TLC switch its official trip-data format from CSV to Parquet?
options: CSV format was permanently discontinued by all software
Parquet files are required by federal law for transportation data
There was no real technical reason for the switch
Smaller files, faster reads, and a schema built directly into the file
questions.explain: This mirrors why real-world data engineering pipelines default to Parquet whenever possible.

questions.q: What does 'schema-on-write' mean in the context of Parquet?
options: Data is written first, and the schema is generated later by a separate tool
The schema is determined and saved into the file at the time it's written, not re-derived every time it's read
The schema can only be changed by rewriting the entire dataset from scratch
It refers to writing CSV files with an inferred schema
questions.explain: This is the direct contrast with CSV's inferSchema, which re-derives types on every single read.
